description:
Trigger: the Google log_list.json schema can carry a log with `state.rejected` set (a log the browser/CT operator has explicitly removed from trust). The parser at log_list.rs:193-227 only inspects `state.usable` and `state.retired`; any other state — `pending`, `qualified`, `readonly`, `rejected` — is silently treated as 'present-but-state-unknown' and the log is inserted with `usable_from_ms = None`, `retired_at_ms = None`.

Actual bad behavior: a 'rejected' log — explicitly distrusted by the browser program that publishes the list — is imported as a trusted CT log. Combined with PKIX-ppbr.1 (the None-passes-window-check bug), any SCT signed by that log's key verifies successfully. The CT log list is the trust-anchor seam for SCT verification; importing a rejected log is the equivalent of importing a rejected root CA into the trust store.

Compounding factor: this is silent. There is no log-level diagnostic, no warning, no skipped-log counter. A consumer reading 'parsed N logs, all verified consistent' from `from_google_log_list_json` has no way to know that some of those N logs are explicitly distrusted.

Fix: explicitly handle each state variant. At minimum, skip logs whose state is `pending`, `qualified`, `rejected`. Treat `readonly` as usable with a stored `retired_at_ms` if the timestamp is present. Document the policy in the rustdoc for `from_google_log_list_json`.
title: from_google_log_list_json silently imports 'rejected' and other non-usable logs as trusted
